title: Austrian Pine: Ancient Austrian Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Pinus nigra shrugs off bad soil. The Opatovice Pine in a Moravian chateau park, about 250 years old, is locally called the six-headed dragon.
intro: Austrian pine, Pinus nigra, is a Mediterranean and Balkan species that nineteenth-century cities across two continents planted for exactly what it does best: shrug off compacted, disturbed ground that would stunt almost anything else. The oldest here grows in the chateau park of Velke Opatovice in Moravia, about 250 years old, its trunk splitting into five stems just above the ground and one of those into three more, which is why locals call it the six-headed dragon. Montreal's, just inside the gate of Notre-Dame-des-Neiges cemetery, took its tolerance sideways instead of up, spreading eighteen metres wide on a trunk barely half as tall. Portland's grows out of a street planter a florist put in before the street existed and has reached 31 metres. Vienna's has been a protected natural monument since 1942 with no age ever recorded.
